Appendix VIII
THE TITHI-NITYĀS
(in the Samaya reckoning)

**1. Bright half of the lunar month**

| Day | Presiding deity | Name of Day | Name of Night (Candra-kalā) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Pādya | Kāmeśvarī | Samjñānā | Darśā |
| 2. Dritīya | Bhaga-mālini | vijñānā | Dṛṣṭā |
| 3. Tṛtīya | Nitya-klinna | Prjñāna | darśitā |
| 4. Caturthi | Bheruṇḍā | Jānat | Viśva-rupa |
| 5. Pañcami | Vahni-vāsinī | Abhijānat | Sudarśanā |
| 6. Shasṭi | Mahā-vajreśvarī | Samkalpa-mānā | Āpyāyāmānā |
| 7. Saptami | Śiva-dūti | Prakalpa mānā | Āpyāyamānā |
| 8. Aṣṭami | Tvaritā | Upakalpamānā | Apyāyā |
| 9. Navami | Kula-sundarī | Upa-klptā | Sūnṛta |
| 10. Daśami | Nityā | Klptā | lrā |
| 11. Ekādaśī | Nīla-patākā | Śreyas | Āpūryamānā |
| 12. Dvādaśī | Vijayā | Vaśīyas | Āpūryamānā |
| 13. Trayodaśī | Sarva-mangalā | Āyat | Pūrayanti |
| 14. Caturdaśī | Jvālā-malini | Sambhūtā | Pūrņā |
| 15. Paurņami | Citrā | Bhūtā | Paurņāmasī |

**2. Dark half of the lunar month**

| Day | Presiding deity | Name of Day | Name of Night (Candra-kalā) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Pādya | Citrā | Prastutā | Sutā |
| 2. Dritīya | Jvālā-mālinī | viṣṭutā | Sunṛtā |
| 3. Trīya | Sarva-mangalā | Samstutā | Prasutā |
| 4. Caturthi | Vijayā | Kalyāņā | Sūyamānā |
| 5. Pañcami | Nīla-patākā | Viśva-rūpā | Abhiṣūyāmānā |
| 6. Shasṭi | Nityā | Śukrā | Priti |
| 7. Saptami | Kula-sundarī | Amṛtā | Prapā |
| 8. Aṣṭami | Tvaritā | Tejasvi | Sampā |
| 9. Navami | Śiva-dūti | Tejas | Tṛpti |
| 10. Dasami | Mahā-vajreśvarī | Samiddhā | Tarpayanti |
| 11. Ekādaśī | Vahni-vāsinī | Aruṇa | Kāntā |
| 12. Dvadasi | Binerundā | Bhānumat | Kāmyā |
| 13. Trayodaśī | Nitya-klinnā | Marīci-mat | Kāma-jātā |
| 14. Caturdaśī | Bahga-mālinī | Abhi-tapat | Āyuṣmatī |
| 15. Amāvāsya | Kāmeśvarī | Tapasvit | Kāma-dughā |
summary: This appendix, titled "THE TITHI-NITYĀS", provides a detailed list of deities and names associated with each lunar day (tithi) within the "Samaya reckoning". It is divided into two sections: the bright half (Śukla Pakṣa) and the dark half (Kṛṣṇa Pakṣa) of the lunar month. For each of the 15 tithis in both halves, the appendix specifies the presiding Nityā deity, a unique name for the day, and a unique name for the night, known as the Candra-kalā.
purpose: The purpose of this appendix is to serve as a reference guide that correlates each of the 30 lunar days (tithis) of a month with its specific presiding deity, a name for the day, and a name for the night, according to the Samaya tradition. This information is relevant for ritualistic, astrological, or scholastic practices within this context.
key_information: The appendix lists the Tithi-Nityās, which are the presiding deities for each day of the lunar cycle.
It covers both the bright half (Śukla Pakṣa) and the dark half (Kṛṣṇa Pakṣa) of the lunar month.
For each tithi, it provides the presiding deity, a specific "Name of Day", and a specific "Name of Night (Candra-kalā)".
The data is presented according to the "Samaya reckoning", a specific tradition or system of calculation.
The list of presiding deities is cyclical, with the same set of 15 Nityās governing the tithis of both halves of the month, though in a different order for the dark half.

tables_and_data.description: Two tables listing the associations for each of the 15 tithis in the bright and dark halves of the lunar month. Each table has four columns: 'Day' (the name of the tithi), 'Presiding deity', 'Name of Day', and 'Name of Night (Candra-kalā)'.
tables_and_data.data_summary: The tables map each tithi to a specific deity and unique names for the day and night. For instance, the first day of the bright half (Pādya) is overseen by Kāmeśvarī, with the day named Samjñānā and the night Darśā. In contrast, the first day of the dark half (Pādya) is overseen by Citrā, with the day named Prastutā and the night Sutā. The list completes the full 30-day lunar cycle, ending with the new moon (Amāvāsya) which is presided over by Kāmeśvarī.
